_about:
Pin-catalog seed list. Every lib_id in `lib_ids` gets its pin map loaded from the live .kicad_sym library and injected into the architect system prompt. The architect LLM then knows the EXACT pin names for those parts and never has to guess (e.g. 'is it NRST or RESET on STM32?'). On retry, the catalog auto-extends with any new lib_ids the previous attempt mentioned, so the LLM gets the pin map for parts it tried but mis-pinned.

This is the single biggest fix to LLM pin hallucination per published research (PCBSchemaGen arXiv 2602.00510, CircuitLM arXiv 2601.04505). Add new lib_ids here when you want them always-available; restart the server to pick up changes.
_enabled_comment: Set false to disable the catalog injection (returns to vanilla prompt). Useful for A/B comparing retry rates.
_max_pins_comment: Cap on the pin-listing length per part. Raised to 100 (2026-06-02) so 48/64/100-pin MCUs show their FULL pinout — at cap=32 even the 48-pin STM32F103C8Tx was truncated, so the architect never saw pins past #32 and had to guess crystal/peripheral pins, causing PIN_NOT_ON_SYMBOL build failures. 100 covers LQFP-100 parts; raise further for BGA-144/176 if needed (watch prompt budget). The '+N more' fallback still applies beyond the cap.
_include_etype_comment: When true, each pin is rendered as 'NAME(NUM, etype)' — e.g. 'VCC(8, power_in)'. The etype helps the LLM avoid wiring an output to power. Set false to shrink the catalog if prompt size matters.
_skip_aliases_comment: Pin names matching these are dropped from the catalog (they're noise for the LLM). KiCad uses '~' for unnamed pins on simple parts like resistors/caps; 'NC' is no-connect.
